edits.current:
When a host callback result contains a selected checked `Subtype`, pass a
`LeanBridge::YourModule::Runtime::Callback` instead of a bare CODE reference:

```perl
my $callback = LeanBridge::YourModule::Runtime::Callback->new(
    code => sub { $_[0]->copy->badd(1) },
    recovery => Math::BigInt->new(1),
);
my $result = LeanBridge::YourModule::call_host($callback);
```

The recovery has the callback's exact erased result shape. The adapter validates
and copies it before Lean or the callback runs, then Lean applies the selected
constructor to the callback's actual result. An invalid recovery prevents the
CODE reference from running. An invalid result or Perl exception preserves the
first failure, suppresses later callbacks in that call and leaves the runtime
usable. The recovery only completes Lean's failure path; it is not returned as
success. A returned Lean closure with checked `Subtype` arguments needs no
recovery. Its `call` validates those arguments first, preserves rejected caller
values and remains usable until `close`.

## Directional callback Subtypes in C, C++ and Perl

Run the installed C-family matrix with the pinned Lean compiler and native build
dependencies:

```sh
source scripts/env.sh
LEAN_BRIDGE_CALLBACK_SUBTYPE_NATIVE_PROFILES=c,cpp \
  node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/callback-subtype-native-installed.test.mjs
```

The test builds ordinary-source and independently reviewed packages, verifies
the package-set receipt, deletes each author root, installs from the copied
handoff and runs independent C11/GMP and C++20 consumers. It checks exact typed
host-result recovery, invalid recovery before callback entry, constructor
rejection after callback entry, mixed arguments, returned-closure input
rejection, unchanged outputs, disposal and reuse after failure. The default
record is `build/callback-subtypes/native.json`.

Run the complete CPAN matrix only after preparing all four pinned interpreters:

```sh
source scripts/env.sh
LEAN_BRIDGE_CALLBACK_SUBTYPE_PERL_TEST=1 \
  node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/callback-subtype-perl-installed.test.mjs
```

This runs ordinary and reviewed packages on threaded and unthreaded Perl 5.36.3
and 5.38.2, through both prebuilt-only and local XS installation. All sixteen
cells delete author inputs, install offline, relocate the installed tree, remove
the handoff, execute twice and verify every installed-file hash. The consumer
adds nested `Except (Option Subtype)` host results and `Array (Option Subtype)`
closure inputs, exception identity and idempotent close. The default record is
`build/callback-subtypes/perl.json`.

The recurring hosted entry points are
`scripts/run-callback-subtype-native-ci.sh` and
`scripts/run-callback-subtype-perl-ci.sh`. They refuse environment variables
that could narrow the matrix, force one build thread and the glibc 2.38 package
floor, retain terminal TAP and the original report, and run an independent
checker bound to the exact producer commit. Their workflows upload complete or
partial output on every exit and then fail the job if acceptance did not pass.

edits.current: C and C++ packages check `Fin` and selected `Subtype` arguments of a returned Lean closure before invoking it, including supported copied containers and mixed refined/unrefined arguments. They also preserve refined values that Lean produces as closure results or host-callback arguments. A returned closure rejects an invalid argument with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; C++ throws `Error`. For a host callback result containing a selected `Subtype`, the host supplies one typed recovery value before the call: the C callback descriptor's `recovery` pointer or C++ `with_recovery(callback, value)`. The public wrapper validates and copies that value before Lean or the callback runs. Lean independently runs the selected checked constructor on every host-produced refined leaf. A rejected recovery prevents the callback from running; a rejected callback result records the first error, suppresses later callbacks and leaves the caller's output unchanged. The recovery exists only so Lean can finish its failure path and is never returned as success. Ordinary and independently reviewed packages exercise the same direction and exact constructor choices. Nested callbacks, retained or asynchronous callbacks, checked-record callback positions, owned callback Subtypes and other native targets remain separate work.
edits.previous: C and C++ packages check `Fin` arguments of a returned Lean closure before invoking it, including bounds inside structural containers, plain records and variants. They also preserve bounded values that Lean produces as closure results or host-callback arguments. A returned closure rejects an argument at or above its bound with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; C++ throws `Error`. The Lean adapter independently constructs each `Fin` from a decidable proof and returns `none` on rejection. It never substitutes a default Fin. `Fin 0` rejects every value. Ordinary C/C++ host callbacks can return Fin inside a shape with a Fin-free failure value, such as `Option (Fin 5)` or `Array (Fin 5)`. The C wrapper checks bounds before conversion; Lean independently reconstructs bounded values from decidable proofs. A rejected reply preserves the first error, suppresses later host callbacks and leaves the caller's output unchanged. Lean may continue internally with a typed Fin-free placeholder, so this is not a rollback guarantee. Bare Fin replies, replies whose selected failure constructor requires a Fin, callback Subtype, checked records, nested callbacks and refined ordinary arguments beside callbacks remain rejected. Reviewed host replies need separate installed acceptance. Other native targets require their own adapters.
